### Method reminder

A mutation is a sudden, random change in a gene or chromosome. It is different from normal growth, fertilisation or DNA copying.

### Solution

A mutation is a **sudden change in the structure or amount of genetic material** (a gene or chromosome). Growth, fertilisation and DNA replication are normal processes that do not change the genetic code. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: A sudden change in the amount or structure of the genetic material
A gradual change in an organism's size as it grows
The joining of a sperm and an egg
The copying of DNA before cell division

enonce_markdown: Which pair contains only mutagens (agents that can cause mutations)?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Common mutagens are ionising radiation (X-rays, gamma rays), ultraviolet light and some chemicals such as mustard gas.

### Solution

X-rays are ionising radiation and mustard gas is a mutagenic chemical. Oxygen, starch and fibre are not mutagens. **Answer: D.**

enonce_markdown: A farmer working in the sun develops a mutation in one skin cell caused by ultraviolet light. Why will this mutation NOT be passed on to his children?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Only mutations in cells that form gametes (sperm or egg cells) can be inherited by the next generation.

### Solution

Skin cells are body cells. The mutation can pass to new skin cells from that cell, but not to children, because children develop from gametes. A mutation in a gamete would be inherited. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Mutations caused by ultraviolet light are always reversed
The mutation is in a body cell and not in a gamete
Only mutations caused by chemicals can be inherited
Skin cells do not contain DNA

enonce_markdown: Sickle-cell anaemia is an inherited disease. Which statement correctly explains its origin?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A gene mutation changes the instructions for making a protein. If the mutation is in a gamete, it can be inherited.

### Solution

Sickle-cell anaemia results from a mutation in the **haemoglobin gene**, which gives abnormal haemoglobin. It is not an infection and it is not caused by diet, although iron deficiency causes a different type of anaemia. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: It is caused by a bacterium in the blood
It is caused by a lack of iron in the diet
It is caused by a virus passed from mother to child
It arose from a mutation in the gene that codes for haemoglobin

enonce_markdown:
A hospital radiographer takes X-ray images every day.

(a) Explain why repeated exposure to X-rays is harmful.

(b) State **two** precautions that protect the radiographer.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

X-rays are ionising radiation. They damage DNA in cells (mutation), which may lead to cancer, and the dose is reduced by shielding, distance and short exposure.

### Solution

(a) X-rays are ionising radiation. They damage the DNA of cells and cause **mutations**. Mutations in body cells can cause uncontrolled cell division (cancer); mutations in gametes can be passed to children.

(b) Any two of: standing behind a lead screen or wearing a lead apron; wearing a dosimeter badge to monitor exposure; limiting the time of exposure and keeping a distance from the X-ray source.

enonce_markdown:
Scientists exposed batches of 1000 fruit flies to different doses of X-rays and counted the mutants.

| Dose (arbitrary units) | 0 | 10 | 20 | 40 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mutants per 1000 flies | 2 | 8 | 14 | 26 |

Assuming the same pattern continues, how many mutants per 1000 flies are expected at a dose of 30 units?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Look for the pattern in a table: find the change in the result for each equal change in dose, then apply it.

### Solution

From 0 to 10 units the count rises by 6 (2 to 8), from 10 to 20 by 6 (8 to 14), and from 20 to 40 by 12 (14 to 26), which is again 6 per 10 units. At 30 units: $2 + 3 \times 6 = 20$ mutants per 1000. A higher dose of radiation causes more mutations. 17 and 23 come from misjudging the mid-point, and 32 continues the pattern beyond 40 units. **Answer: B.**
